title: Iter Aenēae · Module 3 (Troy to Sicily)

ports.name: Trōia
ports.title: Troy has fallen
ports.story: After ten years of war, the Greeks break Troy open and its towers burn. Out of the ruins comes Aeneas, a Trojan prince. The gods tell him to find a new home in the west, in Italy. He gathers the survivors and builds a fleet.

ports.name: Mare Nostrum
ports.title: Out on “Our Sea”
ports.story: The fleet sets out across the great sea the Romans called Mare Nostrum, “Our Sea.” The voyage will be long and uncertain.

quote.latin:
Arma virumque canō, Trōiae quī prīmus ab ōrīs
Ītaliam fātō profugus Lāvīniaque vēnit
lītora, multum ille et terrīs iactātus et altō
quote.english: I sing of arms and the man who first came from the shores of Troy, an exile driven by fate, to Italy and the shores of Lavinium; much was he tossed about on land and on the deep sea.
quote.meaning: These are the poem's first words. Aeneas did not choose this voyage: fate sent him. The whole Aeneid is about a man who keeps going because it is his duty.

ports.name: Venus
ports.title: Venus watches over the fleet
ports.story: Venus, goddess of love, is Aeneas's own mother. She guards and guides him toward Italy.

quote.latin: Tantae mōlis erat Rōmānam condere gentem.
quote.english: So great a labor it was to found the Roman people.
quote.meaning: Vergil wants his readers to feel what Rome cost: storms, losses, years at sea. Great things take great effort, and the gods' quarrels make it harder still.

ports.name: the storm
ports.title: A storm in the dark
ports.story: Juno, queen of the gods, hates the Trojans and never lets them rest. Out on the open sea, a storm wraps the fleet in darkness for three days and nights, until even the helmsman cannot tell day from night. Aeneas holds his course, the way a Roman hero should.
ports.english: Juno does not love the sailors.

quote.latin: ō passī graviōra, dabit deus hīs quoque fīnem.
quote.english: O you who have suffered worse things, a god will grant an end to these too.
quote.meaning: Aeneas is as tired and frightened as his men, but he speaks to give them courage. Leading others through hardship is part of his duty.

ports.name: Sicilia
ports.title: Land at last: Sicily
ports.story: After years of wandering, the battered fleet reaches the island of Sicily. Here Aeneas's old father, Anchises, dies. Italy is close now, but Juno is not finished: her greatest storm is still to come.

quote.latin:
forsan et haec ōlim meminisse iuvābit.
Per variōs cāsūs, per tot discrīmina rērum
tendimus in Latium, sēdēs ubi Fāta quiētās
ostendunt; illīc fās rēgna resurgere Trōiae.
quote.english: Perhaps one day it will be a joy to remember even these things. Through many misfortunes, through so many dangers, we are heading for Latium, where the Fates show us a peaceful home; there Troy’s kingdom is destined to rise again.
quote.meaning: This is why they endure: the hardships have a purpose. A long, hard road leads to a new home, and one day even the storms will be worth remembering.

questions.q: In “Puella nautam videt,” who is doing the seeing?
questions.why: Puella ends in -a: it is the subject.

questions.q: The sailor sees the island: “Nauta ___ videt.”
questions.why: The island receives the action, so it takes -am.

questions.q: Which ending marks ONE object (accusative singular)?
Which ending marks MORE THAN ONE subject (nominative plural)?
Translate: “Nautae aquam vident.”
questions.why: Nautae (-ae) is the subject; aquam (-am) is the object.

questions.q: In “Iūnō nautās nōn amat,” what is nautās?
What does “Venus nautās amat” mean?
questions.why: Nautās is the object, and -ās means more than one.

questions.q: What does “Iūnō nautās nōn amat” mean?
options: Juno does not love the sailors.
The sailors do not love Juno.

questions.q: What does silva mean?
What does via mean?
What does terra mean?
What does īnsula mean?
The woman sees the road: “Fēmina ___ videt.”
The sailors see the land: “___ terram vident.”
In “Terram nauta videt,” which word is the object?
questions.why: -am marks the object, even when it comes first.

questions.q: Translate: “Puellae silvās vident.”
Is nauta masculine or feminine?
questions.why: A sailor was a man, even though the word looks like the others.

questions.q: Translate: “Īnsulam puella videt.”
questions.why: The endings decide, not the word order.

questions.q: The Romans called the Mediterranean Mare Nostrum. What does that mean?
Which goddess protects Aeneas?
questions.why: Juno hates the Trojans; Venus is Aeneas's mother.
